BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r1.claim: After Abraham perfected himself, he perfected others through a gracious recommendation of what benefits them, whether religious or worldly.
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r1.anchor: لما كمل إبراهيم عليه السلام في نفسه كمل غيره بالتوصية وهو تقديم ما فيه خير وصلاح

BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r2.claim: ‘It’ refers to the religion in the preceding mention of Abraham’s way.
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r2.anchor: بالملة المذكورة في قوله تعالى : {ومن يرغب عن ملة إبراهام}

BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r3.claim: Some count Abraham’s eight sons as Ishmael by Hājar, Isaac by Sarah, and six sons by Keturah: Midian, Midain, Zimran, Yaqshan, Yashbaq, and Nuh.
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r3.anchor: أولاده الذكور الثمانية عند البعض إسماعيل وأمه هاجر القبطية وإسحاق وأمه سارة وستة أمهم قنطورا

BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r4.claim: Jacob also advised his twelve sons; the commentary names them and explains his name by saying he followed his twin Esau out of the womb holding his heel.
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r4.anchor: أيضا وهو ابن إسحاق بن إبراهيم بنيه الاثني عشر

BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r5.claim: A birth story has the twins speak in the womb: Esau demands to emerge first, Jacob yields to avoid harming their mother, and Jacob comes out holding Esau’s heel; Esau grows harsh and hunts, Jacob gentle and pastoral.
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r5.anchor: تكلما في بطنها وهي تسمع فقال أحدهما للآخر

BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r6.claim: Jacob and Esau reportedly died on the same day and were buried together; Jacob lived 147 years, died in Egypt, and asked Joseph to bury him in the Holy Land by Isaac.
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r6.anchor: وروي أنهما ماتا في يوم واحد ودفنا في قبر واحد

BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r7.claim: The vocative ‘my sons’ is governed by an understood verb of saying, since Basran grammarians do not allow a full sentence to be the object except with verbs of thought or speech.
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r7.anchor: على إضمار القول عند البصريين تقديره وصى

BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r8.claim: God chose Islam as the purest religion; the prohibition against dying except as Muslims really commands steadfastness in Islam, sincere monotheism, and good expectation of God, since people cannot control death.
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r8.anchor: دين الإسلام الذي هو صفوة الأديان ولا دين عنده غيره

BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r9.claim: Jacob stressed this to his sons after seeing Egyptian idol worship; he singled out his beloved family to show Islam’s priority and because a sound leader’s family helps make the community sound.
BURSEVI:v1p190#2/r9.anchor: وذلك حين دخل يعقوب مصر فرأى أهلها يعبدون الأصنام فأوصى بنيه بأن يثبتوا على الإسلام

QASHANI:2:130-132/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:130-132/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:130-132/r4.claim: The religion Abraham and Jacob enjoined on their sons is the word of unity; Jacob emulated Abraham in advising his sons.

QASHANI:2:130-132/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:130-132/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:130-132/r5.claim: God's chosen religion is the monotheist's divine religion; there is no separate religion or self, for God's religion and essence are one.
QASHANI:2:130-132/r5.anchor: أي: دينه الذي يدين به الموحد، لا دين له غيره، ولا ذات، فدينه دين الله وذاته ذات الله

QASHANI:2:130-132/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:130-132/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:130-132/r6.claim: Dying only as Muslims means not dying the natural death of ignorance, but remaining dead to self and alive through God until bodily death.
QASHANI:2:130-132/r6.anchor: إلا على هذا الدين، أي: لا تموتن بالموت الطبيعي موت الجهل، بل كونوا ميتين بأنفسكم

QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r7.claim: Although their legal practices differed, Abraham and Jacob taught their sons the same undivided foundation of monotheism and Islam.
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r7.anchor: فشرائعهم - وإن اختلفت في الأفعال - فالأصل واحد

QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r8.claim: God’s choosing the religion for them is glad tidings that strengthens their desire, since they can expect divine aid to make obedience easier.
QUSHAYRI:v1p70/r8.anchor: بشارة بما تقوي به دواعيهم على الرغبة فيما يكلفهم من الإسلام

SULAMI:v1p67#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p67#2/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p67#2/r1.claim: Abraham's testament urged his sons to surrender; in sacrificing his son he submitted without looking toward the child, until God ransomed him.
SULAMI:v1p67#2/r1.anchor: قيل اوصاهم بالمجاوبة إلى الاستسلام الذي امر به فصح من إبراهيم

TUSTARI:2:132/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:132/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:132/r1.claim: God requires worship and piety according to people's capacity and knowledge of Him; “fear Him as He deserves” means as much as one can, not permission to abandon piety.
TUSTARI:2:132/r1.anchor: وإنما تعبد الله الخلق على حسب طاقاتهن

TUSTARI:2:132/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:132/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:132/r2.claim: Remaining Muslim means surrendering to God's command and entrusting oneself to Him at all times; others are left to reasoning, so the same wording can carry a particular or general meaning.
TUSTARI:2:132/r2.anchor: أي مسلمون لأمر الله بكل حال مفوضون إليه

TUSTARI:2:132/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:132/r3.speaker: سهل
TUSTARI:2:132/r3.claim: If the Godfearing prayed against wrongdoers, all generations would perish; instead, God made them a mercy through whom He rescues wrongdoers.
TUSTARI:2:132/r3.anchor: قال أبو بكر: ثم قال سهل: لو دعا المتقون على المسرفين لهلك الأولون

TUSTARI:2:132/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:132/r4.speaker: سهل
TUSTARI:2:132/r4.claim: The most honored before God are the Godfearing; whoever seeks His honor should fear Him to attain honor, Paradise, nearness, and great success.
TUSTARI:2:132/r4.anchor: فإن أكرم الخلق على الله عز وجل المتقون

TUSTARI:2:132/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:132/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:2:132/r5.claim: Whoever reforms his inward state has his outward state reformed by God; whoever fears Him inwardly is brought near.
TUSTARI:2:132/r5.anchor:
وقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" من أصلح سريرته أصلح الله علانيته

AKHFASH:v1p158/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p158/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p158/r1.claim: ويعقوب is understood as beginning a new quotation, وقال يعقوب يا بني, because وصى بها already indicates that Ibrahim said something.
AKHFASH:v1p158/r1.anchor: فهو - والله اعلم - "وقال يعقوب يا بني" لانه حين قال {ووصى بهآ} قد أخبر انه قال لهم شيئا

AKHFASH:v1p158/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p158/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p158/r2.claim: Alternatively, يعقوب can be coordinated as an object of وصى, followed by an explanation of what Yaqub said.
AKHFASH:v1p158/r2.anchor: وان شئت قلت {ويعقوب} معطوف كأنك قلت: "ووصى بها ابراهيم بنيه ويعقوب" ثم فسر ما قال يعقوب

FARRA:v1p78/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p78/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p78/r7.claim: Medinan copies read وأوصى in place of وصى; both forms are sound and frequent in Arabic.
FARRA:v1p78/r7.anchor: في مصاحف أهل المدينة «وأوصى» وكلاهما صواب

FARRA:v1p78/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p78/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p78/r8.claim: ويعقوب is a second subject: Jacob also enjoined this teaching.

FARRA:v1p78/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p78/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p78/r9.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh or Ubayy inserts أن before the address; the canonical reading omits it, since reported speech may take or omit أن.
FARRA:v1p78/r9.anchor: وفي إحدى القراءتين قراءة عبد الله أو قراءة أبي: «أن يا بني إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين»

MAJAZ:v1p56/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p56/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p56/r3.claim: اصطفى لكم الدين means He made the religion pure for you, from the root صفوة.
MAJAZ:v1p56/r3.anchor: أي أخلص لكم الدين، من الصفوة

NAHHAS:v1p264/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r1.claim: A geminated وصّى suggests multiplicity and is therefore a less suitable reading here; better is to treat وصّى and أوصى as synonyms, like كرّمنا and أكرمنا.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r1.anchor: فيه معنى التكثير وإذا كان كذلك بعدت القراءة به وأحسن من هذا أن يكون وصى وأوصى بمعنى واحد

NAHHAS:v1p264/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r2.claim: Ibrahim is nominative as the verb’s subject, and Yaʿqub is coordinated with him.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r2.anchor: إبراهيم ) رفع بفعله ( ويعقوب ) عطف عليه

NAHHAS:v1p264/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r3.claim: يا بني is a construct vocative; its first-person yāʾ is fatḥa because sukūn would meet another sukūn, as in بمصرخي.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r3.anchor: يا بني ) نداء مضاف وهذه ياء النفس لا يجوز ههنا إلا فتحها

NAHHAS:v1p264/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r4.claim: إن is read with kasra after the verb of advising and saying; an alternative supplies an omitted verb of saying.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r4.anchor: إن الله ) كسرت إن لأن أوصى وقال واحد وقيل على إضمار القول

NAHHAS:v1p264/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r5.claim: فلا تموتن is jussive prohibition emphasized by heavy nūn; wāw drops where two sukūns meet.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r5.anchor: فلا تموتن ) في موضع جزم بالنهي أكد بالنون الثقيلة وحذفت الواو لالتقاء الساكنين

NAHHAS:v1p264/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p264/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p264/r6.claim: إلا وأنتم مسلمون is a subject-predicate clause used circumstantially.
NAHHAS:v1p264/r6.anchor: إلا وأنتم مسلمون ) ابتداء وخبر في موضع الحال

IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r1.claim: Abraham counseled his sons to adhere to Islam, God’s religion.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس : ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه قال : وصاهم بالاسلام وصية الله دين الله

IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r2.claim: Jacob gave his sons the same counsel to follow Islam; al-Hasan and Qatada report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r2.anchor: به عن ابن عباس : ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه ويعقوب قال : وصى يعقوب بنيه بمثل ذلك - يعني - بالاسلام

IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r3.speaker: طاوس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r3.claim: They should remain in Islam and under its covenant until death.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p239#2/r3.anchor: عن طاووس فلا تموتن الا وأنتم مسلمون على الاسلام وعلى ذمة الاسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r1.claim: People of truth preserve their teaching for successors, urging them not to deviate from a precious legacy gained through struggle and time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r1.anchor: من سننهم التوصية لمن يظنونهم خلفا عنهم في الناس بأن لا يحيدوا عن طريق الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r2.claim: A testament is a beneficial command or prohibition whose loss causes harm, stronger than an ordinary instruction and used when loss is feared, especially at death or before travel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r2.anchor: والإيصاء أمر أو نهي يتعلق بصلاح المخاطب خصوصا أو عموما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r3.claim: The Prophet's counsel to al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriya drew such emotion that companions asked for a farewell-like testament; his final counsel to Muʿadh before Yemen was to treat people well; another questioner was told not to become angry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r3.anchor: وعظنا رسول الله موعظة وجلت منها القلوب وذرفت منها العيون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r4.claim: Abraham and Jacob may have delivered this testament at death, as 2:133 suggests, or at another time when they feared their teaching might be lost.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r4.anchor: فوصية إبراهيم ويعقوب إما عند الموت كما تشعر به الآية الآتية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r5.claim: The pronoun in wa-waṣṣā bihā refers either to the religion or to the declaration aslamtu li-rabbi l-ʿālamīn in 2:131, which condenses the religion's meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r5.anchor: والضمير المجرور بالباء عائد على الملة أو على الكلمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r6.claim: Abraham had eight sons: Ishmael by Hagar, Isaac by Sarah, and six by Keturah; the Torah details little about the latter sons except Midian's lineage and Moses' refuge there, where Jethro or Reuel was priest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r6.anchor: وبنو إبراهيم ثمانية : إسماعيل وهو أكبر بنيه وأمه هاجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r7.claim: Jacob, son of Isaac and Rebekah, lived during Abraham's lifetime, was named Israel and ancestor of Israelites, died in Egypt, and was buried at Machpelah in Canaan beside his forebears.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p727/r7.anchor: وأما يعقوب فهو ابن إسحاق من زوجه رفقة الأرامية تزوجها سنة ست وثلاثين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read awṣā (“enjoined”) instead of waṣṣā; both mean the same, though waṣṣā suggests repeated or emphatic instruction.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r3.claim: The pronoun in “with it” may refer to Abraham's statement “I submit to the Lord of the worlds” or the preceding religion; Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the nearer statement.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r4.speaker: عمرو بن فائد الأسواري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r4.claim: ʿAmr b. Fāʾid reads Yaʿqūb in the accusative, including Jacob among those who enjoined their children; other grammarians coordinate him with Abraham or treat him separately as saying “My sons.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r5.claim: Iṣṭafā here means choosing the purest religions; al-dīn refers to the already known religion. Inna is kasra after waṣṣā because it represents quoted speech, and Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read an yā banī with an explicit particle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r5.anchor: الألف واللام في الدين للعهد، لأنهم قد كانوا عرفوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r6.claim: “Do not die except as Muslims” concisely commands Islam and perseverance: since one knows death will come but not when, one must remain constantly upon the command. Antum muslimūn is a circumstantial nominal clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p213/r6.anchor: فإذا أمر بأمر لا يأتيه الموت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and the Medinans read awṣā with alif and a light ṣād, while the other codices/readers have waṣṣā without alif and with doubled ṣād; the author links this to differences between Medinan and Iraqi codices, listing twelve variants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r1.anchor: قرأ بان عباس وأهل المدينة وأوصى بألف مع تخفيف الصاد والباقون بغير ألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r2.claim: Waṣṣā is more emphatic than awṣā because it can indicate repeated acts of counsel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r2.anchor: ووصى أبلغ من اوصى لأنها تكون لمرات كثيرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r3.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Zajjaj say the pronoun in “with it” refers to the matter of counsel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r3.anchor: وهاء بها تعود على المسألة قاله عكرمة و الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r4.claim: Muqatil counts Abraham’s sons as four: Ishmael, Isaac, Midian, and Mada'in.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل وبنوه أربعة إسماعيل وإسحاق ومدين ومدائن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p148#3/r5.claim: Other authorities say Abraham’s sons numbered eight.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p149/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p149/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p149/r1.claim: The command not to die except as Muslims means to remain committed to Islam so that death finds one upon it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p149/r1.anchor: يريد الزموا الإسلام فاذا أدرككم الموت صادفكم عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r2.claim: The pronoun in 'he enjoined it' refers either to Abraham's religion of submission to God or to the statement, 'I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.'
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r2.anchor: أي: وصى بهذه الملة (2) وهي الإسلام لله [أو يعود الضمير على الكلمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r3.claim: Abraham and Jacob lovingly preserved the religion until death and enjoined it on their descendants, as with the lasting word in 43:28.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r3.anchor: لحرصهم عليها ومحبتهم لها حافظوا عليها إلى حين الوفاة ووصوا أبناءهم بها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r4.speaker: بعض السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r4.claim: Some early readers put Yaqub in the accusative, coordinated with Abraham's sons, meaning Abraham also enjoined his grandson Yaqub, who was present.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r4.anchor: وقد قرأ بعض السلف "ويعقوب" بالنصب عطفا على بنيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r5.speaker: القشيري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r5.claim: Al-Qushayri, as quoted by al-Qurtubi, claims Yaqub was born only after Abraham died; Ibn Kathir says this needs sound evidence and holds that Yaqub was likely born during Abraham and Sarah's lifetime.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r5.anchor: أن يعقوب إنما ولد بعد وفاة إبراهيم، ويحتاج مثل هذا إلى دليل صحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r6.claim: The wording about the promise of Isaac and, after Isaac, Yaqub implies Yaqub existed in Abraham's lifetime; naming him among Isaac's descendants would otherwise have little point, and 29:27 and 21:72 also say God granted Abraham Yaqub.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r6.anchor: فلو لم يوجد يعقوب في حياتهما لما كان لذكره من بين ذرية إسحاق كبير فائدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir also notes the earlier books' identification of Yaqub as builder of Jerusalem and the Prophetic report that Jerusalem followed the Sacred Mosque by forty years; Ibn Hibban's chronology tying Solomon's rebuilding directly to Abraham is rejected as spanning thousands of years.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r7.anchor: وأيضا فإنه باني بيت المقدس، كما نطقت بذلك الكتب المتقدمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r8.claim: The following account of Jacob's own charge to his children supports reading him here among those who enjoined the faith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446/r8.anchor: وأيضا فإن ذكر وصية يعقوب لبنيه سيأتي ذكرها قريبا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446#2/r1.claim: The command means to live rightly and remain steadfast so God grants death in that state; people generally die and are resurrected in the condition they followed, and God makes good intentions easier to fulfill.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446#2/r1.anchor: أحسنوا في حال الحياة والزموا هذا ليرزقكم (5) الله الوفاة عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446#2/r2.claim: This does not contradict the sound hadith about one whose final recorded destiny overtakes deeds near the end, since some versions clarify that the contrary deeds were only what appeared to people; 92:5–10 describes God's facilitation toward outcomes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p446#2/r2.anchor: "فيعمل بعمل أهل الجنة فيما يبدو للناس، ويعمل بعمل أهل النار فيما يبدو للناس.

SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r1.claim: وصى is read as وصى, intensive in view of the recipients, or as quadriliteral أوصى by Nafi and Ibn Amir, matching Madinan and Syrian codices; some say both mean the same.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r1.anchor: قرىء من وصى، وفيه معنى التكثير باعتبار المفعول الموصى، وأوصى رباعيا

SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r2.claim: Zamakhshari says بها refers to the clause أسلمت لرب العالمين construed as a word or sentence, like the feminine pronoun in جعلها كلمة.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " والضمير في " بها " لقوله { أسلمت لرب العالمين } على تأويل الكلمة والجملة،

SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the word implied by أسلمت because it is the nearest antecedent; the author corrects the Sheikh's attribution, since Zamakhshari also gave this analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r3.anchor: الثاني: أنه يعود على الكلمة المفهومة من قوله " أسلمت " كما تقدم تقريره

SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r4.claim: Other antecedents proposed for بها are the later implied word in فلا تموتن, the word of faith, obedience, or the testament implied by وصى; بها attaches to وصى and بنيه is its object.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132/r4.anchor: الرابع: أنه يعود إلى كلمة الإخلاص وإن لم يجر لها [ذكر]. الخامس: أنه يعود

SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r1.claim: Most read ويعقوب nominative and coordinate it with إبراهيم, supplying an omitted object, his sons; another nominative parse makes it a subject with omitted predicate قال.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r1.anchor: الجمهور على رفعه وفيه قولان، أظهرهما: أنه عطف على " إبراهيم " ويكون مفعوله

SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r2.speaker: إسماعيل بن عبد الله وعمرو بن فائد
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r2.claim: They read ويعقوب accusative, coordinating it with بنيه: Abraham enjoined Jacob too.

SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r3.claim: يا بني may be Abraham's speech under either the preferred coordination or accusative reading, or Jacob's speech if he is parsed as a new subject, with Abraham's words omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما: أنه من مقول إبراهيم، وذلك على القول بعطف يعقوب على إبراهيم

SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r4.speaker: البصريون
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r4.claim: Basrans supply an omitted قال before يا بني; Kufans attach the speech to وصية because testament has the force of saying.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r4.anchor: على رأي البصريين، أي: فقال يا بني، وبفعل الوصية

SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud's أن يا بني reading supports treating the following words as an explanatory clause, not a verbal noun; Kufans who reject that call أن extra.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r5.anchor: ويؤيد تعلقها بالوصية قراءة ابن مسعود: " أن يا بني " ب " أن " المفسرة،

SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r6.claim: يعقوب is a foreign proper name and therefore indeclinable; deriving it from birth after Esau or numerous descendants wrongly makes it an Arabic derivation that should decline.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r6.anchor: ومن زعم أنه سمي يعقوب لأنه ولد عقب العيص أخيه

SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r7.claim: يعقوب also names a partridge and, as a masculine name from that word, would decline; اصطفى's alif derives through yāʾ from the root waw.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r7.anchor: ويعقوب أيضا ذكر الحجل، إذا سمي به المذكر انصرف، والجمع يعاقبة

SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r8.claim: لكم means لأجلكم, and the definite article in الذين is referential.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#2/r8.anchor: و " لكم " أي لأجلكم، والالف واللام في " الذين " للعهد.

SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r1.claim: فلا تموتن formally forbids dying but really forbids being outside Islam at death, like forbidding prayer except with humility; the wording marks death without Islam as unworthy.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r1.anchor: هذا نهي في الصورة عن الموت، وهو في الحقيقة نهي عن كونهم على خلاف حال الإسلام

SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r2.claim: تموتن derives from تموتونن: the indicative nūn is dropped before emphatic nūn, then waw is deleted at the sukūn junction and its damma remains as a trace.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r2.anchor: وأصل تموتن: تموتونن: النون الأولى علامة الرفع والثانية المشددة للتوكيد

SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r3.claim: إلا وأنتم مسلمون is a total exception of states; the nominal clause is accusative as a circumstantial, governed by the verb before إلا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:132#3/r3.anchor: هذا استثناء مفرغ من الأحوال العامة، و " أنتم مسلمون " مبتدأ وخبر في محل نصل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r1.claim: A reading has wa-awṣā, found in the codices of the Hijaz and Syria.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r1.anchor: قرىء ( واوصى ) وهي في مصاحف اهل الحجاز والشام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r2.claim: The pronoun in bihā refers to Abraham’s ‘I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds,’ construed as a word or sentence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r2.anchor: والضمير في ﴿ بها ﴾ لقوله ﴿ أسلمت لرب العالمين ﴾ على تأويل الكلمة والجملة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r3.claim: The feminine pronoun is supported by calling the statement a lasting word in the parallel Abraham passage.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r3.anchor: ونحوه رجوع الضمير في قوله ﴿ وجعلها كلمة باقية ﴾ الزخرف 28

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r4.claim: With Yaʿqūb nominative, he is coordinated with Abraham and shares the ruling: Jacob also enjoined his sons.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r4.anchor: ﴿ ويعقوب ﴾ الزخرف 26 - 27 عطف على إبراهيم داخل في حكمه والمعنى ووصى بها يعقوب بنيه أيضا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r5.claim: An accusative reading of Yaʿqūb coordinates him with the sons: Abraham enjoined his sons and grandson.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r5.anchor: وقرىء ( ويعقوب ) بالنصب عطفا على بنيه ومعناه ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه ونافلته يعقوب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r6.claim: The vocative yā-bunayya is governed by an implied ‘he said’ for Basrans; Kufans attach it to waṣṣā because that verb means ‘said.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r6.anchor: على إضمار القول عند البصريين وعند الكوفيين يتعلق بوصى لأنه في معنى القول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r7.claim: Abū and Ibn Masʿūd read the vocative with an explicit an.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217/r7.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي وابن مسعود ( أن يا بني )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.claim: God chose Islam for Abraham’s descendants as the best religion and enabled them to follow it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.anchor: أعطاكم الدين الذي هو صفوة الأديان وهو دين الاسلام ووفقكم للأخذ به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.claim: The prohibition is really against dying in a state other than Islam; it does not prohibit death itself, and marks death outside steadfast Islam as devoid of good.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.anchor: فلا يكن موتكم الا على حال كونكم ثابتين على الإسلام فالنهي في الحقيقة عن كونهم على خلاف حال الاسلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.claim: The same wording can forbid prayer without humility: formally it addresses prayer to emphasize that prayer without humility is no prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.anchor: لا تصل الا وانت خاشع فلا تنهاه عن الصلاة ولكن عن ترك الخشوع في حال صلاته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.claim: A Prophetic saying says that a neighbor of the mosque has no prayer except in the mosque, illustrating the construction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.anchor: ألا ترى إلى قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام 57 ( لا صلاة لجار المسجد الا في المسجد )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.claim: Likewise, ‘die as a martyr’ means be in the state of martyrs when death comes, acknowledging that death’s honor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.anchor: وتقول في الأمر أيضا مت وانت شهيد وليس مرادك الأمر بالموت ولكن بالكون على صفة الشهداء اذا مات

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r7.claim: The feminine pronoun in “he enjoined it” refers to Abraham's religion, mentioned immediately before.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r8.claim: Waṣṣā is stronger than awṣā: awṣā could be said once, while waṣṣā implies repeated counsel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r8.anchor: ووصى أبلغ من أوصى , لأن أوصى يجوز أن يكون قاله مرة واحدة , ووصى لا يكون إلا مرارا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r9.claim: Abraham advised his sons and Jacob later advised his sons that God chose Islam for them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r9.anchor: والمعنى أن إبراهيم وصى , ثم وصى بعده يعقوب بنيه , فقالا جميعا : { يا بني إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r10.claim: The prohibition against dying as anything but Muslim means to adhere to Islam and not leave it before death, not to forbid death itself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p192/r10.anchor: لأن النهي توجه إلى مفارقة الإسلام , لا إلى الموت , ومعناه : الزموا الإسلام ولا تفارقوه إلى الموت

MUQATIL:2:130-134/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:130-134/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:130-134/r3.claim: God’s command “submit” means be sincere, and Abraham’s “I submit” means sincere to the Lord of the worlds; Abraham charged four sons and Jacob his twelve sons to keep Islam and die as sincere monotheists.
MUQATIL:2:130-134/r3.anchor: { إذ قال له ربه أسلم } ، يقول: أخلص، { قال أسلمت } ، يعنى أخلصت

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r1.speaker: مدني
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r1.claim: The Medinan reading has أوصى instead of وصى.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r2.speaker: شامي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r2.claim: The Syrian reading likewise has أوصى instead of وصى.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r3.claim: The pronoun بها refers either to the religious community or to the declaration أسلمت لرب العالمين.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r3.anchor: بالملة أو بالكلمة وهى أسلمت لرب العالمين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r4.claim: Yaʿqūb is coordinated with Abraham and therefore also commanded his sons to keep this religion.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r4.anchor: هو معطوف على إبراهيم داخل فى حكمه والمعنى ووصى بها يعقوب بنيه أيضا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r5.claim: God selected Islam as the finest religion and enabled them to adopt it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r5.anchor: أعطاكم الدين الذى هو صفوة الأديان وهو دين الإسلام ووفقكم للأخذ به

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r6.claim: The prohibition is not to die except while steadfast in Islam; it forbids being in another state at death, as a command not to pray except humbly forbids lack of humility.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71#4/r6.anchor: الإسلام إذا ماتوا كقولك لا تصل إلا و أنت خاشع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r1.claim: Ibrahim advised his sons to follow the religious community; al-Qurṭubī prefers this over identifying it with the nearer phrase أسلمت لرب العالمين, which would mean to say we have submitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r1.anchor: أي بالملة وقيل: بالكلمة التي هي قوله: { أسلمت لرب العالمين } وهو أصوب لأنه أقرب مذكور،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r2.claim: وصى and أوصى are synonymous dialect forms used by Quraysh and others, and both are recited.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r2.anchor: ووصى وأوصى لغتان لقريش وغيرهم بمعنى مثل كرمنا وأكرمنا وقرىء بهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r3.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allāh has وصى; the ʿUthmānic codex and the readings of Medina and Syria have أوصى, while the remaining readers have وصى, which carries an intensive sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r3.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله «ووصى»، وفي مصحف عثمان «وأوصى» وهي قراءة أهل المدينة والشام.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r4.claim: ويعقوب may be coordinated with Ibrahim as another adviser, or treated as a new clause in which Jacob later advises his own sons.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r4.anchor: رفع بفعله، «ويعقوب» عطف عليه وقيل: هو مقطوع مستأنف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r5.claim: Ishmael was Hajar's eldest son, whom Ibrahim took to Mecca as an infant; reports give ages of two or fourteen, but al-Qurṭubī says infancy is correct.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r5.anchor: وبنو إبراهيم: إسماعيل، وأمه هاجر القبطية، وهو أكبر ولده نقله إبراهيم إلى مكة وهو رضيع.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r6.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r6.claim: Reports differ on Ishmael's age when brought to Mecca: two years or fourteen years.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r6.anchor: وقيل: كان له سنتان وقيل: كان له أربع عشرة سنة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r7.claim: Ishmael was born fourteen years before Isaac, died at 137 or, in another report, 130, and was 89 when Ibrahim died.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r7.anchor: وولد قبل أخيه إسحق بأربع عشرة سنة، ومات وله مائة وسبع وثلاثون سنة. وقيل: مائة وثلاثون.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r8.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r8.claim: Some identify Ishmael as the son offered for sacrifice; al-Qurṭubī prefers Isaac as the more correct view, to be discussed in al-Ṣāffāt.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r8.anchor: وهو الذبيح في قول. وإسحق أمه سارة، وهو الذبيح في قول آخر، وهو الأصح،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r9.claim: Isaac's descendants include Romans, Greeks, Armenians, and Israelites; Isaac lived 180 years and was buried with Ibrahim in the Holy Land.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r9.anchor: ومن ولده الروم واليونان والأرمن ومن يجري مجراهم وبنو إسرائيل. وعاش إسحق مائة وثمانين سنة،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r10.claim: After Sarah's death Ibrahim married Qantura, daughter of Yaqtan the Canaanite, and had Midian, Midan, Nahshan, Zamran, Nashiq, and Shuyukh; his death preceded the Prophet's birth by about 2,600 years, while Jewish chronology subtracts about 400.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r10.anchor: ثم لما توفيت سارة تزوج إبراهيم عليه السلام قنطورا بنت يقطن الكنعانية، فولدت له مدين ومداين ونهشان وزمران

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r11.claim: Jacob's children will be named in Sūrat Yūsuf.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r11.anchor: وسيأتي ذكر أولاد يعقوب في سورة «يوسف»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r12.speaker: عمرو بن فائد الأسواري وإسماعيل بن عبد الله المكي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r12.claim: They read ويعقوب in the accusative, coordinating him with إبراهيم's sons and making Jacob someone Ibrahim advised.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r12.anchor: وقرأ عمرو بن فائد الأسواري وإسماعيل بن عبد الله المكي: «ويعقوب» بالنصب عطفا على «بنيه»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r13.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r13.claim: He considers the accusative reading remote: Jacob was not among Ibrahim's sons or alive to hear the advice, though Jacob also advised his own children.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r13.anchor: قال القشيري: وقرىء «يعقوب» بالنصب عطفا على «بنيه» وهو بعيد لأن يعقوب لم يكن فيما بين أولاد إبراهيم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r14.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r14.claim: He reports that Jacob, seeing Egyptians worship idols, fire, and cattle, gathered his sons out of concern and asked what they would worship after him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r14.anchor: قال الكلبي: لما دخل يعقوب إلى مصر رآهم يعبدون الأوثان والنيران والبقر،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r15.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r15.claim: A folk etymology says Jacob was named for grasping his twin Esau's heel at birth; al-Qurṭubī doubts it because the name is foreign, despite coinciding with an Arabic bird name.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132/r15.anchor: ويقال: إنما سمي يعقوب لأنه كان هو والعيص توأمين، فخرج من بطن أمه آخذا بعقب أخيه العيص.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r1.claim: Jacob lived 147 years, died in Egypt, and asked to be buried beside Isaac in the Holy Land; Joseph carried him there.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r1.anchor: عاش عليه السلام مائة وسبعا وأربعين سنة ومات بمصر، وأوصى أن يحمل إلى الأرض المقدسة،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r2.claim: يا بني means أن يا بني; Ubayy, Ibn Masʿūd, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read the phrase with أن.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r2.anchor: معناه أن يا بني وكذلك هو في قراءة أبي وابن مسعود والضحاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r3.claim: He says أن is omitted because a testament functions like speech; speech-related clauses allow it either to appear or be omitted, and he rejects the grammarians' explanation that it was intended but elided.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: ألغيت أن لأن التوصية كالقول، وكل كلام يرجع إلى القول جاز فيه دخول أن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r4.claim: He parses يا بني as a vocative with the possessive yāʾ opened to avoid two adjoining quiescent letters, like بمصرخي.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r4.anchor: النحاس: «يا بني» نداء مضاف، وهذه ياء النفس لا يجوز هنا إلا فتحها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r5.claim: إن is read with kasra because وصى and قال function as speech, or alternatively because an implicit speech verb is understood.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r5.anchor: إن الله } كسرت «إن» لأن أوصى وقال واحد. وقيل: على إضمار القول.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r6.claim: اصطفى means chose; the rajaz line illustrates the form.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#2/r6.anchor:
اصطفى } اختار. قال الراجز:
يا بن ملوك ورثوا الأملاكا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r1.claim: الدين means Islam, and the definite article refers to the religion already known to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r1.anchor: لكم الدين } أي الإسلام والألف واللام في «الدين» للعهد لأنهم قد كانوا عرفوه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r2.claim: The concise command means remain committed to Islam and never leave it until death; its brevity both conveys the command and warns of death, whose time is unknown.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r2.anchor: الزموا الإسلام ودوموا عليه ولا تفارقوه حتى تموتوا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r3.claim: The order is a prohibition with emphatic nūn; تموتن is jussive and loses its waw because two quiescent letters meet.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r3.anchor: «لا» نهي «تموتن» في موضع جزم بالنهي، أكد بالنون الثقيلة، وحذفت الواو لالتقاء الساكنين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r4.claim: إلا وأنتم مسلمون is a subject-predicate clause functioning circumstantially; مسلمون is also explained as having good hope in God, sincere, surrendered, or believing.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:132#3/r4.anchor: «إلا وأنتم مسلمون» ابتداء وخبر في موضع الحال أي محسنون بربكم الظن،

RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r1.claim: Nafi’ and Ibn Amir read awṣā with an alif, as in Medina and Syrian codices; the others read waṣṣā with gemination, suggesting emphasis and repetition though the meaning is alike.
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر ( وأوصى ) بالألف وكذلك هو في مصاحف المدينة والشام

RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r2.claim: The pronoun may refer to Abraham’s statement “I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds,” understood as a word or sentence; the feminine form is supported by “a word enduring.”
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r2.anchor: أنه عائد إلى قوله : { أسلمت لرب العالمين } ( البقرة : 131 ) على تأويل الكلمة

RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r3.claim: The Qadi prefers that the pronoun refer to Abraham’s religion: it has an explicit antecedent and is broader than a single profession of faith, encompassing what secures success in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r3.anchor: قال القاضي وهذا القول أولى من الأول من وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r4.claim: Calling it a testament rather than an order makes the charge more emphatic because concern for religion intensifies as death approaches.
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r4.anchor: لفظ الوصية أوكد من الأمر ، لأن الوصية عند الخوف من الموت

RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r5.claim: Abraham addressed his sons because a father’s care for them is especially strong, showing how seriously he regarded the faith.
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r5.anchor: وذلك لأن شفقة الرجل على أبنائه أكثر من شفقته على غيرهم

RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r6.claim: He included all his sons without exception, which further signals his intense concern.
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r6.anchor: عمم بهذه الوصية جميع بنيه ولم يخص أحدا منهم بهذه الوصية

RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r7.claim: The unbounded command and prohibition against dying outside Islam require constant adherence, since death may come at any moment.
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r7.anchor: أطلق هذه الوصية غير مقيدة بزمان معين ومكان معين

RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r8.claim: Abraham included no other testament, signaling that this was his foremost concern; although he specially addressed family, he invited all people to Islam.
RAZI-FULL:v4p66/r8.anchor: ما مزج بهذه الوصية وصية أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r1.claim: Most read “and Jacob” as coordinated with Abraham, meaning Jacob gave the same testament; an accusative reading coordinates it with “his sons” and includes his grandson Jacob in Abraham’s testament.
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r1.anchor: الأول : وهو الأشهر أنه معطوف على إبراهيم

RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r2.claim: The vocative “O my sons” is an implied quotation for Basran grammarians and governed by “testament” as a speech act for Kufans; Ubayy and Ibn Masud read it with the particle ya.
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r2.anchor: فهو على إضمار القول عند البصريين ، وعند الكوفيين يتعلق بوصي لأنه في معنى القول

RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r3.claim: God chose the religion by establishing clear proofs, calling them to it, and keeping them from other religions.
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r3.anchor: استخلصه بأن أقام عليه الدلائل الظاهرة الجلية ودعاكم إليه

RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r4.claim: The command not to die except as Muslims requires embracing Islam at every moment, because death may arrive before a person later turns to it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p66#2/r4.anchor: إذا لم يأمن الموت في كل طرفة عين ، ثم إنه أمر بأن يأتي بالشيء قبل الموت

STUDYQURAN:2:131/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:131/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:131/r1.claim: The theme of submission begun in 2:128 continues through Abraham, Jacob, and their children.
STUDYQURAN:2:131/r1.anchor: from v. 128 continues through to Jacob and his children

STUDYQURAN:2:131/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:131/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:131/r2.claim: Islām is Muhammad’s religion by proper name, but the Quran also uses it for primordial true religion and a universal orientation of the soul toward God bequeathed by prophets.
STUDYQURAN:2:131/r2.anchor: generalized in the Quran to imply the primordial religion and true religion as such

TAB-FULL:v2p583/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r1.claim: The waw joins Jacob to Abraham: Jacob also instructed his sons in Islam after Abraham had instructed his sons.
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r1.anchor: يقول: ووصى بها يعقوب بنيه بعد إبراهيم

TAB-FULL:v2p583/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r2.claim: Jacob gave his sons the same testament after Abraham.
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r2.anchor: ووصى بها يعقوب بنيه بعد إبراهيم

TAB-FULL:v2p583/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r3.claim: Abraham and Jacob both instructed their sons in Islam.
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r3.anchor: وصاهم بالإسلام، ووصى يعقوب بمثل ذلك

TAB-FULL:v2p583/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r4.claim: Al-Tabari rejects parsing Abraham’s clause as complete and Jacob’s as a new subject with a different testament; both patriarchs urged obedience, humility, and Islam.
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r4.anchor: ولا معنى لقول من قال ذلك؛ ولأن الذي أوصى به يعقوب بنيه

TAB-FULL:v2p583/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r5.claim: The particle an is omitted because a testament is speech in meaning, so the construction follows the verb say; the verse at 4:11 and poetry illustrate this semantic syntax.
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r5.anchor: لأن الوصية قول فحملت على معناها

TAB-FULL:v2p583/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r6.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r6.claim: Another grammarian says an is omitted because the vocative يا بني suffices, though Arabs sometimes use particles without an and sometimes add it.
TAB-FULL:v2p583/r6.anchor: إنما حذفت أن من قوله: {ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه ويعقوب}

TAB-FULL:v2p584/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p584/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p584/r1.claim: God chose and selected the religion He had already entrusted to Abraham’s descendants; the definite article marks a religion made familiar to them by their ancestors’ testament.
TAB-FULL:v2p584/r1.anchor: قد عرفوه بوصيتهما إياهم به ووصيتهما إليهم فيه

TAB-FULL:v2p585/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p585/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p585/r1.claim: Do not die except as Muslims means never leave Islam during life, since no one knows when death will come; otherwise they may die outside God’s chosen faith under His anger and perish.
TAB-FULL:v2p585/r1.anchor: أي فلا تفارقوا هذا الدين وهو الإسلام أيام حياتكم

TABATABAI:2:132/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:132/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:132/r1.claim: Righteousness has ranks: Abraham still asks to join those who preceded him, and God answers that he belongs among the righteous in the Hereafter.
TABATABAI:2:132/r1.anchor: فإذا تأملت ذلك حق التأمل قضيت بأن الصلاح ذو مراتب بعضها فوق بعض

TABATABAI:2:132/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:132/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:132/r2.claim: He suggests Abraham may have asked to join Muhammad and the Prophet’s purified family, whose higher righteousness he says Muhammad claims for himself.
TABATABAI:2:132/r2.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام سأل اللحوق بمحمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وآله الطاهرين

TABATABAI:2:132/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:132/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:132/r3.claim: The object of Abraham’s bequest to his sons is the religious way, the milla.
TABATABAI:2:132/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى { ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه } ، أي وصى بالملة

TABATABAI:2:132/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:132/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:132/r4.claim: Because death is involuntary, the prohibition means to remain firmly Muslim so death does not find one outside Islam.
TABATABAI:2:132/r4.anchor: النهي عن الموت وهو أمر غير اختياري للإنسان،

TABATABAI:2:133/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:133/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:133/r1.claim: The cited declaration that religion with God is Islam confirms that Islam is the religion Abraham brought and that his descendants inherited.

TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r1.claim: The preceding reports describe the first level of Islam and faith.
TABATABAI:2:130-134#4/r1.anchor: وهي تدل على ما مر بيانه من المرتبة الأولى من الإسلام والإيمان

ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r1.claim: The pronoun in بها refers to Abraham’s religion: his Islam displays his way and practice, as the surrounding wording names Abraham’s community and the chosen religion.
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r1.anchor:
قوله: (بها) هذه الهاء ترجع على الملة، لأن إسلامه هو إظهار طريقته
وسنته ويدل على قوله: (ومن يرغب عن ملة إبراهيم)

ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r2.claim: إن is kasra because وصى/أوصى introduces the words spoken to them: ‘God has chosen the religion for you.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r2.anchor:
وإنما كسرت " إن) لأن معنى وصي وأوصى: قول: المعنى
قال لهم إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين،

ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r3.claim: وصّى is stronger than أوصى: the latter can describe one admonition, while وصّى implies repetition.
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r3.anchor:
ووصى أبلغ من أوصى، لأن أوصى
جائز أن يكون قال لهم مرة واحدة، ووصى لا يكون إلا لمرات كثيرة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r4.claim: The apparent command not to die uses broad Arabic idiom, like ‘do not let me see you here’; it really tells the addressee not to remain there.
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r4.anchor:
هذا جملى سعة الكلام، وما تكثر استعماله " العرب " نحو قولهم: " لا أرينك
ههنا "، فلفظ النهي

ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r5.claim: The verse means to remain committed to Islam so that death finds them as Muslims.
ZAJJAJ:v1p211/r5.anchor: المعنى: لا تكونن ههنا فإن من كان ههنا - رأيته - والمعنى في الآية: ألزموا الإسلام،

TABRISI:2:132/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام
TABRISI:2:132/r1.claim: The Medinan and Syrian readers use وأوصى with hamza and a light ṣād.
TABRISI:2:132/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والشام وأوصى بهمزة بين واوين وتخفيف الصاد

TABRISI:2:132/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:2:132/r2.claim: The other readers use ووصى with a doubled ṣād.

TABRISI:2:132/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:132/r3.claim: The doubled form is supported by توصية as the verbal noun of وصى; a doubled form here would produce an impermissible cluster of three yāʾs.
TABRISI:2:132/r3.anchor: فتوصية مصدر وصى مثل قطع تقطعة

TABRISI:2:132/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:132/r4.claim: The hamza reading is supported by God's wording يوصيكم الله and من بعد وصية توصون بها.
TABRISI:2:132/r4.anchor: حجة من قرأ وأوصى بها إبراهيم قوله يوصيكم الله

TABRISI:2:132/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:132/r5.claim: وصى and أوصى mean the same as command and charge; the root also describes joined parts of a house.

TABRISI:2:132/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:2:132/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda parse Jacob as coordinated with Abraham: both charged their sons with this faith.
TABRISI:2:132/r6.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:2:132/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:132/r7.claim: The coordination with Abraham is clearer because it requires no omitted words; the alternative treats Jacob as beginning a new clause with an implied charge.
TABRISI:2:132/r7.anchor: والأول أظهر والفرق بين التقديرين أن الأول لا إضمار فيه

TABRISI:2:132/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132/r8.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:132/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the pronoun in بها refers to the milla, while another view takes it to refer to the statement أسلمت لرب العالمين.
TABRISI:2:132/r8.anchor: وهو قول الزجاج وقيل إنها تعود إلى الكلمة التي هي أسلمت لرب العالمين

TABRISI:2:132/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:132/r9.claim: The definite expression الدين refers specifically to the known religion of Islam, not religion in general.
TABRISI:2:132/r9.anchor: والألف واللام في الدين للعهد دون الاستغراق لأنه أراد دين الإسلام

TABRISI:2:132/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:132/r10.claim: The prohibition against dying except as Muslims actually commands them not to abandon Islam, so death will find them adhering to it; Arabic لا أرينك here has the same indirect force.
TABRISI:2:132/r10.anchor: فالنهي على الحقيقة عن ترك الإسلام لئلا يصادفهم الموت عليه

TABRISI:2:132#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:132#2/r1.claim: The phrase بها may refer to the enduring word of monotheism, as supported by the statement that God made it a lasting word, or to the declaration of faith لا إله إلا الله.
TABRISI:2:132#2/r1.anchor: وقيل بكلمة الإخلاص وهي لا إله إلا الله

TABRISI:2:132#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:132#2/r2.claim: Ibrahim addressed his sons because his concern for them was greater and they were especially likely to accept his charge, although he called all people to Islam.
TABRISI:2:132#2/r2.anchor: إنما خص البنين لأن إشفاقه عليهم أكثر وهم بقبول وصيته أجدر

TABRISI:2:132#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:132#2/r3.claim: Jacob, son of Isaac, was named Yaʿqūb because his twin ʿĪṣ preceded him at birth and Yaʿqūb followed holding his heel.
TABRISI:2:132#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس والمعنى ووصى يعقوب بنيه الاثني عشر

TABRISI:2:132#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:132#2/r4.claim: Jacob charged his twelve sons, the tribes, that God had chosen Islam for them.
TABRISI:2:132#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى ووصى يعقوب بنيه الاثني عشر وهم الأسباط

TABRISI:2:132#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:132#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the instruction as remaining committed to Islam so that death finds them Muslim.
TABRISI:2:132#2/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج معناه الزموا الإسلام فإذا أدرككم الموت صادفكم مسلمين

TABRISI:2:132#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:132#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:132#2/r6.claim: The verse encourages a person approaching death to instruct dependents to fear God and keep to religion and obedience.
TABRISI:2:132#2/r6.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على الترغيب في الوصية عند الموت

THALABI:v1p279/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p279/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p279/r6.claim: Abdullah's codex reads fa-wassa; Medina and Syria read awsa, as Abu Ubayd also saw in Uthman's codex; the rest read the doubled form, two synonymous ways to command someone.
THALABI:v1p279/r6.anchor: ووصى في مصحف عبد الله: فوصى، وقال أهل المدينة والشام: وأوصى بالألف

THALABI:v1p279/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p279/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p279/r7.claim: The pronoun in biha can refer to the declaration that there is no god but God, the religion, or the testament; al-Mufaddal also supplies an implicit obedience, supported by idiom and poetry.
THALABI:v1p279/r7.anchor: الكلبي ومقاتل: يعني كلمة الآحاد لا إله إلا الله

THALABI:v1p279/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p279/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p279/r8.claim: Ibrahim's sons included Ishmael by Hajar and Isaac by Sarah, and children by Qatura, whom he married after Sarah died.
THALABI:v1p279/r8.anchor: إسماعيل وأمه هاجر القبطية، وإسحاق وأمه سارة

THALABI:v1p279/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p279/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p279/r9.claim: Jacob was named because his twin Esau came out first and Jacob followed, holding his heel; another view derives the name from his many descendants.
THALABI:v1p279/r9.anchor: لأنه والعيص كانا توأمين فتقدم عيص في الخروج من بطن أمه وخرج يعقوب على أثره فأخذ يعقبه. قاله ابن عباس

THALABI:v1p279/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p279/r10.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v1p279/r10.claim: A prophetic report says he was sent after eight thousand prophets, four thousand of them from the Children of Israel.
THALABI:v1p279/r10.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «بعثت على أثر ثمانية آلاف نبي أربعة آلاف من بني إسرائيل

THALABI:v1p280/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p280/r1.claim: Jacob also passed on the testament to his twelve sons, whom the commentary lists by name.
THALABI:v1p280/r1.anchor: ويعقوب: بنيه الأثني عشر وهم روفيل أكبر ولده وشمعون

THALABI:v1p280/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p280/r2.claim: Ya bani means O my sons, with Abi and Ibn Masud reading an explicit an; al-Farra supplies an omitted he said because a testament is speech, supported by Qur'anic idiom and poetry.
THALABI:v1p280/r2.anchor: يا بني معناه أن يا بني، وكذلك في قراءة أبي وابن مسعود

THALABI:v1p280/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r3.speaker: ابن مجاهد
THALABI:v1p280/r3.claim: He transmits a reading that connects Jacob as a coordinate with the sons, since Jacob himself belongs among those giving the testament.
THALABI:v1p280/r3.anchor: وحكى ابن مجاهد عن بعضهم ويعقوب أيضا نسقا على بنيه

THALABI:v1p280/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p280/r4.claim: God chose Islam for them; dying only as Muslims means believers, sincere, or entrusting themselves to God.
THALABI:v1p280/r4.anchor: إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين اختار لكم الإسلام

THALABI:v1p280/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p280/r5.speaker: الفضيل ابن عياض
THALABI:v1p280/r5.claim: He glosses dying as Muslims as having a good opinion of one's Lord.
THALABI:v1p280/r5.anchor: الفضيل ابن عياض في قوله: فلا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq says inna is kasra because waṣṣā and awṣā mean speech: Abraham said that God had selected the religion for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: إنما كسرت (إن) لأن معنى وصى وأوصى: قول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports Abraham telling his sons not to associate anything with God, even if they were sawn, cut with scissors, or burned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إن إبراهيم قال لبنيه: لا تعدلوا بالله شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r3.claim: The selected religion is Islam, the religion of ḥanīfiyya; its definite article is specific and referential, since Islam was selected over other religions, not the whole genus of religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r3.anchor: يريد: دين الإسلام دين الحنيفية، والألف واللام فيه للعهد لا للجنس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r4.claim: The apparent command not to die is really a command not to abandon Islam, so that death will find them as Muslims; this is like telling someone not to let oneself see them here.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r4.anchor: ووقع النهي في ظاهر الكلام على الموت، وإنما نهوا في الحقيقة عن ترك الإسلام؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj paraphrases the command as remaining firmly Muslim, so that when death arrives it finds them in Islam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: وهذا من سعة الكلام، والمعنى في الآية: ألزموا الإسلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ records the forms of māt: mawta, mayta, and mamāta, noting expressions for barren land, mass death, selling livestock versus other goods, and a person with a lifeless heart.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p343/r6.anchor: قال الفراء في كتاب # المصادر: مات يموت موتا وميتة ومماتا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:131-132/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:131-132/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:131-132/r2.claim: Abraham and Jacob enjoined the religious way, or the word of sincerity, on their sons: Islam, the upright religion chosen by God.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:131-132/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:131-132/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:131-132/r3.claim: “Do not die except as Muslims” means adhere to Islam so death finds you still following it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:131-132/r3.anchor: الزموا الإسلام حتى إذا أدرككم الموت

ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r6.claim: Islam was Abraham's religion from the beginning, and both he and his grandson Jacob enjoined it upon their sons; Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Abu Ja'far read the verb as 'they enjoined.'
ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r6.anchor: Nâfi‘, İbn Âmir, Ebû Ca‘fer kıraatlerinde وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَآ okunur ki vasiyet ettiler demek olur

ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r7.claim: Abraham's sons were Ishmael, Isaac, Midian, and Medan, with other reports giving eight or twenty-four; Jacob had twelve sons, listed here, whose descendants are the Children of Israel.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r7.anchor: İbrâhim’in oğulları: İsmâil, İshâk, Medyen, Medan dört idi. Sekiz veya yirmi dört rivayeti de vardır

ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r8.claim: The fathers tell their sons that God chose for them the purest and most excellent religion to follow, so they must die only as complete Muslims.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#3/r8.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah her hâlde sizin için ittibâ‘olunacak dini bizzat ıstıfâ ve intihab etti

ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r7.claim: The Abraham story and Jacob's testament clarify the meaning of Israel's brothers and the value of Islam.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#6/r7.anchor: kıssa-i İbrâhim’deki kelimâta ve vasiyyet-i Ya‘kūb’a nazar-ı dikkati celb ederek ihvânın mânasını, İslâmın kıymetini tefhim

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r3.claim: Abraham bequeathed the religion to his children and later generations; Jacob repeated the bequest to his sons, charged them to keep monotheism, and received their pledge to continue it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r3.anchor: Hz. Ya‘kub’un da kendi oğullarına aynı vasiyeti tekrar ettiği, tevhid inancından sapmamalarını emrettiği; onların da tevhid geleneğini yaşatacaklarına dair söz verdikleri bildirilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r6.claim: Abraham and Jacob bequeathed a religion that was, in a general sense, Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:130/r6.anchor: İbrâhim’le Ya‘kub’un, oğullarına vasiyet ettikleri din de genel anlamda İslâm’dan başkası değildi

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r1.claim: Nafiʿ and Ibn Amir read وأوصى on Form IV; the other readers use وصى on Form II.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ نافع وابن عامر وأوصى بها على أفعل

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r2.claim: The Form II reading is supported by توصية as the verbal noun of وصى; a Form II noun on tafʿīl would create an unwelcome sequence of three yāʾs, as in the rejected diminutive pattern of عطاء.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r2.anchor: فتوصية مصدر وصى، مثل: قطع تقطعة، ولا يكون فيه تفعيل نحو: التقطيع

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r3.claim: The Form IV reading is supported by يوصيكم الله and وصية; وصى also means that plant parts joined, so a bequest joins the bulk of the testator's affairs to its recipient.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p227#2/r3.anchor: وقد قالوا: وصى النبت: إذا اتصل بعضه ببعض

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p89/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p89/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p89/r1.claim: Arabic readily adapts foreign names when Arabized, a point relevant to the name Ibrahim and its variant forms.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p89/r1.anchor: اتساع العرب في الأسماء الأعجمية اذا عربتها

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p89/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p89/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p89/r2.claim: وصى and أوصى are both read; they differ as Form II and Form IV verbs, a distinction the author says he explained earlier.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p89/r2.anchor: يقرأ بالتشديد من غير ألف وبالتخفيف واثبات الألف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p171/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p171/r3.speaker: نافع، ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p171/r3.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read وأوصى with the additional alif, while the other readers have وصى.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p171/r3.anchor: فقرأ نافع وابن عامر / وأوصى بهآ /

QIRAAT-ER:2:132:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:132:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:132:2#1/r1.claim: The canonical Form IV awṣā reading replaces Form II waṣṣā, shifting from intensified charging to formal bequeathing while keeping the testament sense.
QIRAAT-ER:2:132:2#1/r1.anchor: Canonical Form IV reading changes waṣṣā to awṣā, shifting from intensified charging to formal bequeathing

QIRAAT-ER:2:132:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:132:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:132:4#1/r1.claim: Ibrāhāmu is a canonical adaptation of Ibrahim with long ā in the final syllable, affecting pronunciation and lineage resonance rather than syntax.
QIRAAT-ER:2:132:4#1/r1.anchor: Canonical name-form variant with ā in the final syllable; it affects pronunciation and lineage resonance

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r1.claim: Waṣiyya means an instruction or covenant delivered with admonition about what should be done.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r1.anchor: الوصية: العهد، وصى بنيه: أي عهد إليهم وتقدم إليهم بما يعمل به مقترنا بوعظ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r2.claim: Waṣṣā and awṣā are two forms; the doubled form is said to convey greater emphasis or repeated instruction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p633/r2.anchor: ووصى وأوصى لغتان، إلا أنهم قالوا: إن وصى المشدد يدل على المبالغة والتكثير.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r1.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r1.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read awṣā, while the other readers read waṣṣā; Thalab transmits differences between the Medinan and Iraqi codices.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر: وأوصى، وقرأ الباقون: ووصى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r2.speaker: ثعلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r2.claim: Thalab lists twelve Medinan–Iraqi written/read variants: sārʿū, yaqūl, yartadd, alladhīna ittakhadhū, khayran minhumā/minhā, fatawakkal/tawakkal, an/yuzhir, bimā/fīmā kasabat, tashtahī/tashtahī, al-ghaniyy/huwa al-ghaniyy, and yakhāf/falā yakhāf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r2.anchor: اختلف مصحف أهل المدينة وأهل العراق في اثني عشر حرفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and al-Mahdawi take “by it” to refer to Abraham’s religion, explicitly mentioned nearby.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r3.anchor: وبها متعلق بأوصى، والضمير عائد على الملة في قوله: ومن يرغب عن ملة إبراهيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya initially prefers “the word” that Abraham declared, “I submit to the Lord of the worlds,” because it is the nearest antecedent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r4.anchor: ابتدأ ابن عطية وقال: هو أصوب، لأنه أقرب مذكور،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers “the religion” as antecedent because it is explicit and broader than the word, encompassing what most secures success in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r5.anchor: ورجح العود على الملة بأنه يكون المفسر مصرحا به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r6.claim: Other proposed antecedents for “by it” are the later command to die only as Muslims, the unmentioned but implied confession of faith, the testament itself, or obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r6.anchor: وقيل: يعود على الكلمة المتأخرة، وهو قوله: فلا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r7.claim: Abraham’s sons included Ishmael by Hagar and Isaac by Sarah, plus six sons by Qatura; only Ishmael and Isaac left enduring lines.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p635/r7.anchor: هؤلاء الثمانية ولده لصلبه، والعقب الباقي فيهم اثنان إسماعيل وإسحاق لا غير.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r1.claim: Most readers put Yaʿqūb in the nominative, either coordinating him with Abraham as another who instructed his sons, or making him a subject with an omitted predicate; coordination is clearer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r1.anchor: قرأ الجمهور: ويعقوب بالرفع، وقرأ إسماعيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r2.speaker: إسماعيل بن عبد الله المكي والضرير وعمرو بن فائد الأسواري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r2.claim: These readers put Yaʿqūb in the accusative, coordinating him with “his sons” and taking them as Jacob’s grandsons, since Jacob was Isaac’s son.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r2.anchor: وقرأ إسماعيل بن عبد الله المكي، والضرير، وعمرو بن فائد الأسواري: بالنصب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r3.claim: If Abraham speaks the “O my sons” address, grammarians differ whether an unspoken verb of saying is needed; Kufans treat testament as speech itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r3.anchor: وعند الكوفيين لا يحتاج إلى ذلك، لأن الوصية في معنى القول،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r4.claim: Calling them “my sons” is tender and encourages acceptance, stirring them toward Islam; the statement that God chose the religion makes departure from it irrational.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r4.anchor: وكون النداء بلفظ البنين مضافين إليه تلطف غريب وترجئة للقبول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r5.speaker: أبي وعبد الله والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r5.claim: Ubayy, Abdullah, and al-Dahhak read “an yā banayya”; an is explanatory, while grammarians who reject that use call it redundant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعبد الله والضحاك: أن يا بني،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r6.claim: “God chose the religion for you” means He selected Islam as the purest religion known to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r6.anchor: إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين، أي استخلصه لكم وتخيره لكم صفوة الأديان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r7.claim: “Do not die except as Muslims” means remain in Islam; the apparent ban on dying actually bans being in a state other than Islam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r7.anchor: هذا استثناء من الأحوال، أي إلا على هذه الحالة، والمعنى: الثبوت على الإسلام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r8.claim: The phrasing is concise admonition: because death is certain but its time unknown, the command keeps people mindful and continually in the state in which they should meet death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r8.anchor: وقد تضمن هذا الكلام إيجازا بليغا ووعظا وتذكيرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r9.claim: The command also forbids actions that could cause a person to meet death outside Islam, like “do not let me see you here” really meaning leave the place.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p636/r9.anchor: وهذا على الحقيقة نهي عن تعاطي الأشياء التي تكون سببا للموافاة على غير الإسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r2.claim: The testament shows Abraham’s concern for religion even though his sons already followed Islam, and that he sought their safety in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r2.anchor: ففي ذلك ما كان عليه إبراهيم من الاهتمام بأمر الدين، حتى وصى به من كان ملتبسا به،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r3.claim: He addressed all his sons, without exception, and left the testament unrestricted by time or place, then ended with the strongest warning against dying outside Islam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r3.anchor: ومنها أنه عمم بنيه، ولم يخص أحدا منهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r4.speaker: رسول الله عن النعمان بن بشير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r4.claim: The Prophet challenged al-Nuʿman’s father over a gift to one child, asking whether he wanted equal dutifulness among them and refusing to witness injustice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r4.anchor: حين نحله أبوه شيئا، فقال له رسول الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r5.speaker: المؤرخون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r5.claim: Historians say Ishmael was taken to Mecca as an infant, was fourteen years older than Isaac, and was eighty-nine when Abraham died; Isaac lived 180 years and was buried beside Abraham.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r5.anchor:
قال المؤرخون:
نقل إبراهيم ولده إسماعيل إلى مكة وهو رضيع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r6.speaker: المؤرخون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r6.claim: Historians place about 2,600 years between Abraham’s death and Muhammad’s birth, while Jewish chronology subtracts about 400 years.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p637/r6.anchor: وكان بين وفاة أبيه إبراهيم ومولد محمد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r1.claim: Abraham and Jacob successively bequeathed the hanif religion to their children, continuing the prophets' invitation to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r1.anchor: جعلوا ذلك وصية يوصون بها واحدا بعد واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r2.claim: God's choice of the religion is stated before the testament to make obedience easier and encourage the children to follow it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r2.anchor: وقدم بين يدي وصيته اختيار الله لهم هذا الدين، ليسهل عليهم اتباع ما اختاره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r3.claim: The command not to die except as Muslims urges steadfastness because deeds are judged by their endings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p663/r3.anchor: وأمرهم أنهم لا يموتون إلا عليه، لأن الأعمال بخواتيمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p664/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p664/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p664/r8.claim: The discourse from Abraham's introduction through its close forms one coherent, rhetorically unmatched passage, recalling the challenge to humans and jinn in 17:88.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p664/r8.anchor: كأنها جملة واحدة، في حسن مساقها ونظم اتساقها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r1.claim: Abraham is praised for perfecting others after his own perfection; tawṣiya is urging another toward a beneficial religious act by speech or sign, before death or at another time, and its root connotes joining.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r1.anchor: مدح له عليه السلام بتكميله غيره إثر مدحه بكماله في نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r2.speaker: author
