ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r2.claim: The pronoun in 'with it' most likely refers to the community/religion, since that antecedent is explicit and Jacob's coordination begins a new account of prophets transmitting the true religion; taking it as 'I submitted' has proximity and wording in its favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r2.anchor: ويرجح الأول كون المرجع مذكورا صريحا وكذا ترك المضمر إلى المظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r3.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r3.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read awṣā, with no necessary implication of greater frequency than the form waṣṣā.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع وإبن عامرأوصى ولا دلالة فيها على التكثير

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r4.claim: Yaʿqūb is coordinated with Abraham and is read nominative as a new subject with an omitted predicate meaning 'likewise'; a reading in the accusative coordinates him with Abraham's sons, while making him the implicit agent is remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r4.anchor: ويعقوب عطف على إبراهيم ورفعه على الإبتداء وحذف الخبر أي يعقوب كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r5.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Jacob was named because Esau emerged first and Jacob followed holding his heel; al-Alusi doubts its authenticity.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r5.anchor: وإنما سمى يعقوب لأنه وعيصا كانا توأمين فتقدم عيص وخرج يعقوب على أثره آخذا بعقبه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r6.speaker: البصريون
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r6.claim: Basrans posit an omitted verb of saying before 'O my sons'; it is singular if Jacob is read accusative and dual if he is nominative. Kufans need no ellipsis because testament itself entails speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r6.anchor: يابني على إضمار القول عند البصريين ويقدر بصيغة الأفراد على تقدير نصب يعقوب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads 'an yā banī'; this removes the need for an implicit saying verb for Basrans, and some authorities indicate that adding one is then impermissible.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r7.anchor: وقرأ إبن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه : أن يا بني ولا حاجة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r8.claim: Al-Itqān lists twelve sons of Abraham and twelve of Jacob, naming each group, as historical context for the address to their descendants.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r8.anchor: وبنو إبراهيم على ما في الإتقان إثنا عشر وهم إسماعيل وإسحق ومدين وزمزان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r9.claim: God selected and enabled them for Islam, the religion that is inherently the purest; the wording does not mean Islam is pure only for them, and the term can denote earlier true religion despite later customary restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r9.anchor: إن الله أصطفى لكم الدين أي جعل لكم الدين الذي هو صفوة الأديان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r10.claim: 'Do not die except as Muslims' forbids being in a non-Muslim state at death; although death itself is outside human control, maintaining the state that determines one's death is actionable. The command means remain steadfast in Islam.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r10.anchor: نهى عن الإتصاف بخلاف حال الإسلام وقت الموت والمفهوم من الآية فظاهرا النهي عن الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r11.speaker: الفاضل اليمني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r11.claim: Al-Fāḍil al-Yamanī calls the construction a metaphorical negation of the person to negate a particular state; al-Alusi says negating a person could only negate all attributes, not one state.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r11.anchor: وقال الفاضل اليمني : إن هذا كناية بنفي الذات عن نفي الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r12.claim: Some say the required Islam is inward faith alone because bodily deeds are hardly possible at death, and cite a Prophetic supplication asking that the living be kept Muslim and the dead die in faith; al-Alusi finds this unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p389/r12.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن الإسلام المأمور به هنا ما يكون بالقلب دون العمل بالجوارح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r1.claim: Medinan and Syrian readers have awṣā with an initial alif in their codices; the rest read waṣṣā with gemination, two synonymous forms like anzala and nazzala.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والشام: "وأوصى" بالألف، وكذلك هو في مصاحفهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r2.claim: They say the pronoun refers to the declaration of God's oneness, there is no god but God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: يعني بكلمة الإخلاص لا إله إلا الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r3.claim: He says the pronoun may refer to the religion of Abraham or to the commandment itself.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: إن شئت رددت الكناية إلى الملة لأنه ذكر ملة إبراهيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.claim: Abraham's eight sons are Ishmael, Isaac, and six by Qantura bint Yaqtan; the text identifies Hajar and Sarah as their mothers and says Qantura married Abraham after Sarah died.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r4.anchor: أي وصى إبراهيم بنيه الثمانية إسماعيل وأمه هاجر القبطية، وإسحاق وأمه سارة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.claim: Jacob was a twin with Esau; Esau emerged first, and Jacob followed holding his heel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.anchor: سمي بذلك لأنه والعيص كانا توأمين فتقدم عيص في الخروج من بطن أمه وخرج يعقوب على أثره آخذا بعقبه قاله ابن عباس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r6.claim: Another explanation derives Jacob's name from his many descendants; Jacob also instructed his twelve sons.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: سمي يعقوب لكثرة عقبه يعني: ووصى أيضا يعقوب بنيه الاثني عشر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r7.claim: Yā banī means O my sons; God chose Islam as their religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r7.anchor: {يا بني} معناه أن يا بني {إن الله اصطفى} اختار {لكم الدين} أي دين الإسلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r8.claim: Muslimūn is explained as believers, sincere, or those who entrust themselves; the prohibition appears to target death but really commands steadfastness in Islam until death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r8.anchor: مؤمنون وقيل: مخلصون وقيل: مفوضون والنهي في ظاهر الكلام وقع على الموت،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r9.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r9.claim: He explains being Muslim at death as having a good opinion of one's Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r9.anchor: وعن الفضيل بن عياض رحمه الله أنه قال: {إلا وأنتم مسلمون} أي محسنون بربكم الظن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r10.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r10.claim: Jaber reports that three days before his death the Prophet said no one should die except while holding a good opinion of God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p153#2/r10.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل موته بثلاثة أيام

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r1.claim: Tawṣiya urges another toward a beneficial, pious act; its root suggests connecting the recommender's action to the recipient's, while faṣā means separating.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r1.anchor: التوصية هي التقدم إلى الغير بفعل فيه صلاح وقربة، وأصلها الوصل يقال: وصاه إذا وصله، وفصاه: إذا فصله

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r2.claim: The pronoun in bihā refers either to the religious community or to the statement aslamtu, understood as a word or sentence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r2.anchor: والضمير في بها للملة، أو لقوله أسلمت على تأويل الكلمة، أو الجملة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r3.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r3.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read awṣā in place of waṣṣā; the source judges waṣṣā more emphatic.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وأوصى والأول أبلغ

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r4.claim: Yaqub is coordinated with Abraham as also advising his sons; an accusative reading instead makes him one of those advised by Abraham.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r4.anchor: عطف على إبراهيم، أي ووصى هو أيضا بها بنيه. وقرىء بالنصب على أنه ممن وصاه إبراهيم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r5.claim: Ya banayya is introduced by an implicit saying according to Basran grammarians, but attached to waṣṣā by Kufans as a kind of the same action; a poetic line illustrates the construction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r5.anchor: على إضمار القول عند البصريين، متعلق بوصى عند الكوفيين لأنه نوع منه ونظيره:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r6.claim: The source gives Abraham four sons, or eight, or fourteen; it lists Jacob's twelve sons by name.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r6.anchor: وبنو إبراهيم كانوا أربعة: إسماعيل وإسحاق ومدين ومدان. وقيل: ثمانية. وقيل: أربعة عشر: وبنو يعقوب إثنا عشر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r7.claim: The chosen religion is Islam, the purest religion; the command not to die except as Muslims means remain Muslim until death, not control the moment of dying.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r7.anchor: دين الإسلام الذي هو صفوة الأديان لقوله تعالى: { فلا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون } ظاهره النهي عن الموت على خلاف حال الإسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r8.claim: The wording stresses that dying outside Islam is without good and should not befall them; a parallel command is to die as a martyr.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r8.anchor: وتغيير العبارة للدلالة على أن موتهم لا على الإسلام موت لا خير فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r9.claim: A report says Jews claimed Jacob had enjoined Judaism on his sons at death, and this verse was revealed in response.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:132/r9.anchor: وروي أن اليهود قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ألست تعلم أن يعقوب أوصى بنيه باليهودية يوم مات فنزلت.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r1.claim: After mentioning Abraham's leadership, the author identifies the emulated basis of it as his religion and his testament to his sons, which they transmitted in turn, especially Jacob, the ancestor invoked by the People of Scripture.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r1.anchor: ذكر ما يؤتم به فيه وهو سبب اصطفائه وصلاحه وذلك دينه , وما أوصى به عليه السلام بنيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r2.claim: God chose Abraham because he submitted to his Lord; the omitted object of أسلم encompasses whatever may properly be surrendered to God, and Abraham's submission is to the Lord who benefits all creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r2.anchor: وحذف المفعول ليتناول كل ما يصح إسلامه إلى المسلم إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r3.claim: وصى بها refers to Abraham's words, charge, or chosen quality; the variant وأوصى is from the same testament sense, while the doubled form more strongly conveys repeated and abundant instruction.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r3.anchor: وقرئ ( وأوصى ) فهو من إيصاء والوصية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r4.claim: Abraham and Jacob tell their sons that God chose Islam for them as a mercy, sparing them the search for it; the warning means they must meet death only while wholly surrendered to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r4.anchor: فأغناكم عن تطلبه وإجالة الفكر فيه رحمة منه لكم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r5.claim: The following verses refute the People of Scripture's claims to Judaism or Christianity by demonstrating that Abraham and the prophets were not adherents of those later religions, a falsehood they knew to be false.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r5.anchor: وبرأ خليله والأنبياء من ذلك على وجه أوجب القطع بأنهم عالمون ببطلانه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r6.claim: The author gives the Torah's genealogy of Abraham through Terah and Noah, while noting that Luke's Gospel differs by inserting Cainan in the lineage.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p245/r6.anchor: ذكر في السفر الأول منها أنه إبراهيم بن تارح بن ناحور بن شارغ

BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r1.claim: The Torah narrative says Terah took Abram, Lot, and Sarai from Ur toward Canaan but settled in Haran; after Terah's death, God called Abram at age seventy-five to leave his land and family for the promised land and nationhood.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r1.anchor: وقال الرب لإبرم : اخرج من أرضك من حيث ولدت ومن آل أبيك إلى الأرض التي أريك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r2.claim: Abram migrated with Lot and Sarai to Canaan, built altars at Shechem and Bethel, then famine drove him toward Egypt; fearing the Egyptians would kill him for Sarai, he asked her to say she was his sister, and Pharaoh took her until divine afflictions released her.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r2.anchor: فهبط إبرم إلى مصر ليسكنها لأن الجوع اشتد في الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r3.claim: After leaving Egypt wealthy, Abram returned to Bethel; his and Lot's abundance made the land too small for both, and Lot chose the well-watered Jordan plain compared to God's garden and Egypt.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p246/r3.anchor: ولم تكن تلك الأرض تسعهما كليهما لأن مواشيهما كثرت جدا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p247/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247/r1.claim: Lot settled among the cities around Sodom, whose people were deeply sinful, while Abram stayed in Canaan; God again promised Abram all the land he could see and countless descendants, and Abram settled near Mamre and built an altar.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247/r1.anchor: وكان أهل سدوم أشرارا خطأة جدا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p247/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247/r2.claim: The Torah describes four kings defeating five, taking Lot and Sodom's goods; Abram gathered 318 household men, pursued and defeated them, recovered Lot and the captives, and returned the plunder to Sodom's king.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247/r2.anchor: فعبى فتيانه ومولديه ثلاثمائة وثمانية عشر رجلا وسار في طلبهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.claim: When Abram fears that his steward Eliezer will inherit, God promises an heir from Abram's own body and descendants as numerous as stars; Abram believes, and God covenants to give him the land.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.anchor: لا يرثك هذا بل ابنك الذي يخرج من صلبك فهو يرثك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p247#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247#2/r2.claim: God predicts Abram's descendants will be enslaved for four hundred years, judges their oppressor, and brings them back in the fourth generation after the Amorites' wrongdoing is complete; the covenant land stretches from Egypt to the Euphrates.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.claim: After Sarai gives her Egyptian servant Hagar to Abram because she is barren, Hagar conceives and flees Sarai's harsh treatment; an angel orders her to return and promises many descendants through Ishmael, whose hand will be against everyone and everyone against him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.anchor: فحبلت فقالت سرى لإبرم : أنت صاحب ظلامتي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r1.claim: Ishmael is born when Abram is eighty-six; at ninety-nine God makes a covenant with him, renames him Abraham, promises nations and kings from him, and gives Canaan to his descendants.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r1.anchor: ثم ولدت هاجر لإبرم ابنا فدعا إبرم اسمه إسماعيل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r2.claim: Circumcision is made the covenant's bodily sign for Abraham's household and male descendants: household males are circumcised, boys on the eighth day, and the uncircumcised are cut off for breaking the covenant.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r2.anchor: ويكون علامة العهد بيني وبينكم , وليختن كل ذكر منكم ابن ثمانية أيام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r3.claim: God renames Sarai as Sarah and promises that she will bear Isaac; Abraham laughs at the prospect because he is one hundred and Sarah ninety, then asks that Ishmael live before God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r3.anchor: فخر إبراهيم على وجهه ضاحكا وقال في قلبه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r4.claim: God confirms Isaac as the covenant heir while granting Abraham's request for Ishmael: Ishmael will be blessed, become a great people, and father twelve princes.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p248/r4.anchor: وقد استجبت لك في إسماعيل فباركته وكثرته وأنميته جدا جدا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r1.claim: Abraham circumcises himself at ninety-nine, Ishmael at thirteen, and the household; Sarah later bears Isaac, whom Abraham circumcises on day eight, and celebrates his weaning.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r1.anchor: وكان قد أتى إسماعيل ابنه إذ اختتن ثلاث عشرة سنة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r2.claim: When Sarah demands Hagar and Ishmael's expulsion, Abraham grieves; Hagar loses her water in the wilderness, but God hears the boy, shows her a well, promises him a great people, and Ishmael grows up in Paran as an archer.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r2.anchor: فقال الله لإبراهيم : لا يشقن عليك حال الصبي وأمتك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r3.claim: The Torah account appears to conflict with the sound report that Ishmael was nursing when Abraham left him at the House: the author says the later exile account may fit, while the circumcision at thirteen can be reconciled by miraculous travel to Mecca and back.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح ( أنه وضعه عند البيت وهو يرضع )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r4.claim: The Torah's promises that all earthly peoples will be blessed through Abraham and that Ishmael's hand will be against all are clearer prophecies of Muhammad, the only descendant who fulfilled them; al-Taftazani and al-Samarqandi also noted the passage.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p249/r4.anchor: وفيه بشارة بنبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أصرح مما ذكروه

DURR-FULL:v1p336/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r1.claim: Abraham prescribed Islam for his sons, and Jacob prescribed the same for his sons.
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه} قال: وصاهم بالإسلام ووصى يعقوب بنيه مثل ذلك

DURR-FULL:v1p336/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r2.speaker: فضيل بن عياض
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r2.claim: Fudayl ibn ʿIyad interprets dying only as Muslims as having a good opinion of one's Lord.
DURR-FULL:v1p336/r2.anchor: عن فضيل بن عياض في قوله {فلا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون} أي محسنون بربكم الظن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانتفيهتاءالتأنيث.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانتفيهتاءالتأنيث.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانتفيهتاءالتأنيث.claim: In diminutives of feminine nouns whose ta was added after the stem, Sībawayh drops ta and substitutes hāʾ, the original feminine marker; e.g. بنت becomes بنية and أخت becomes أخية.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانتفيهتاءالتأنيث.anchor: اعلم أنهم يردون ما كانت فيه تاء التأنيث إلى الأصل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانتفيهتاءالتأنيث.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانتفيهتاءالتأنيث.speaker: العرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانتفيهتاءالتأنيث.claim: Some Arabs say هنيهة for the diminutive of هنت and هنية for هن, treating hāʾ as a substitute for yāʾ, as in ذه.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتحقيرماكانتفيهتاءالتأنيث.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول في هنت هنيهة وفي هن هنية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1066/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1066/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1066/r2.claim: As support, he says وصّى is used for religious matters and أوصى for worldly matters such as inheritance, with prayer and alms in 19:31 as the sole religious exception; he also compares كرّم/أكرم.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1066/r2.anchor: يستعمل وصّى في أمور الدين وأوصى في أمور الدنيا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r1.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r1.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r1.claim: Islamic identity can resist cultural loss if adapted to contemporary crises, grounding a new kalām project.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r1.anchor: شريطة أن يكون إطارًا قادرًا على التلاؤم

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r2.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r2.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r2.claim: Control and use of nature have become the main arena of civilizational competition.

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r3.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r3.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r3.claim: Philosophy of science is the necessary entry to contemporary thinking about nature.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r3.anchor: فلسفة العلوم المدخل لهذا باعتبارها التمثيل العيني

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r4.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r4.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r4.claim: New kalām should absorb old kalām's ethical and emotional heritage, then surpass it because its historical conditions have ended.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r4.anchor: جدلية الاستيعاب/التجاوز هي القادرة على شق طريق علم الكلام الجديد

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r5.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r5.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r5.claim: He rejects both passive continuity under ancient authorities and disconnection that leaves the present rootless, favoring a dialectic of connection and separation.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r5.anchor: جدلية الانفصال/الاتصال المنبثقة عن جدلية الاستيعاب/التجاوز

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r6.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r6.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r6.claim: An epistemological break leaves behind an ended phase and its assumptions, sources, and methods for a new stage.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r6.anchor: تنفض اليد تمامًا من مرحلة انتهت، ومن مسلماتها ومصادرها

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r7.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r7.speaker: حسن حنفي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r7.claim: The author compares this break to Ḥasan Ḥanafī's move from enlightenment to revolution, or creed to revolution.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r7.anchor: «د. حسن حنفي» الانتقال من التنوير إلى التثوير

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r8.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r8.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r8.claim: Arabic thāra means agitation; English revolution also evokes a celestial cycle and radical change.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r8.anchor: أما في الإنجليزية فتعني Revolutionary ثوري جذري ودوار

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r9.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r9.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r9.claim: Revolution is effective progress to a higher stage after the former one is exhausted, not sudden emotional rejection.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r9.anchor: لا يجعل الرفض هياجًا انفعاليًّا ومفاجئًا، بل هو تقدم

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r10.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r10.speaker: باشلار
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r10.claim: Bachelard coined epistemological break to describe progress after modern physics overturned Newtonian assumptions.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r10.anchor: ابتدعها «باشلار» ليبلور الوضع التقدمي بعد ثورة العلم العظمي

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r11.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r11.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r11.claim: Classical kalām proved creed; new kalām starts from accepted creed and aims to establish Muslims' presence in history.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r11.anchor: العقيدة المثبتة هي نقطة البدء التي يسلم بها ويسير على أساسها

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r12.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r12.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r12.claim: The proof from origination concerns natural bodies, giving natural science a major role in classical kalām.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r12.anchor: دليل الحدوث أهم الأدلة على وجود الله، والحادث هو الجسم الطبيعي

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r13.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r13.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r13.claim: By the sixth and seventh Islamic centuries, ontology made up half of kalām, including principles, substances, and accidents.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r13.anchor: بلغت نظرية الوجود نصف العلم، وتضم مباحث المبادئ العامة والجواهر والأعراض

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r14.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r14.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r14.claim: Classical kalām moved from epistemology through ontology to theology, isolating natural science in ontology.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r14.anchor: من المعرفة إلى الطبيعيات إلى الإلهيات، أو من الإبستمولوجيا إلى الأنطولوجيا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r15.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r15.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r15.claim: Scientific claims change under testing and correction; methods, the focus of philosophy of science, are more enduring.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r15.anchor: المحتوى في نسق العلم يمثل المتغير الخاضع دومًا للاختبار

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r16.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r16.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r16.claim: Study how scientific thought arose within religious tradition, then shift natural science from ontology to epistemology to serve progress.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r16.anchor: فلنستوعب من تراثنا كيف يبزغ التفكير الطبيعي العلمي

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r17.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r17.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r17.claim: Because new kalām is ideological, it needs a bridge to philosophy of science rather than relocating nature into ideology.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r17.anchor: المطلوب أن نبحث عن حلقة الوصل بينه وبين نظرية علم الكلام الجديد

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r18.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r18.speaker: حسن حنفي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r18.claim: Ḥasan Ḥanafī defines science as philosophical structural study of the human; the external world is understood through people.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r18.anchor: تعريف حسن حنفي للعلم تعريفًا فينومينولوجيًّا بوصفه دراسة بنائية فلسفية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r19.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r19.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r19.claim: Induction has collapsed; modern science starts with creative hypotheses and deduces experimental observations.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r19.anchor: انهار المنهج الاستقرائي الذي يقوم على الملاحظة ثم تعميمها

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r20.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r20.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r20.claim: Science is a succession of successful hypotheses, not discovery of absolute truths.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r20.anchor: فليس العلم اكتشافًا لحقائق مطلقة، بل محض سلسلة من فروض ناجحة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r21.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r21.speaker: هيزينبرج
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r21.claim: Heisenberg calls successive physical theories links in a dialogue between humanity and nature.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r21.anchor: كما يقول «هيزينبرج» النظريات الفيزيائية المتوالية حلقات في سلسلة الحوار

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r22.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r22.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r22.claim: Newton's universe is a deterministic machine in absolute space and time, seemingly erasing the human observer.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r22.anchor: عالم نيوتن آلة ميكانيكية تسير في مسارها المحتوم

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r23.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r23.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r23.claim: Relativity specifies the observer's perspective and speed; quantum observation depends on hypotheses created by the mind.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r23.anchor: ولا تتأتى الملاحظة أصلًا في عالم الكوانتم (الكمومية) بغير فرض

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r24.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r24.speaker: نيلز بور
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r24.claim: Bohr says scientists are not only observers but actors, directors, and authors of science.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r24.anchor: إن العلماء — كما أشار نيلز بور — ليسوا فقط المراقبين أو المشاهدين

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r25.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r25.speaker: مارجوليس
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r25.claim: Margolis calls physical science a human adventure.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r25.anchor: حق قول مارجوليس إن العلوم الفيزيائية محض مغامرة إنسانية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r26.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r26.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r26.claim: He asks whether new kalām can give researchers courage to undertake such scientific adventures.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c6/r26.anchor: يلقي في روعنا العزائم والجسارة لخوض أمثال هذه المغامرات

NASHR:v1p239/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p239/r1.speaker: ابن أبي الهذيل
NASHR:v1p239/r1.claim: Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl reports that they disliked reciting part of a verse and leaving the rest; al-Jazari says the rule applies inside or outside prayer.
NASHR:v1p239/r1.anchor: عن أبي سنان عن ابن أبي الهذيل قال: كانوا يكرهون أن يقرءوا بعض الآية ويدعوا بعضها

NASHR:v1p239/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p239/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p239/r2.claim: Because Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl was a senior Successor and said كانوا, al-Jazari infers that the Companions also disliked partial-verse recitation.
NASHR:v1p239/r2.anchor: وعبد الله بن أبي الهذيل هذا تابعي كبير، وقوله كانوا: يدل على أن الصحابة كانوا يكرهون ذلك

NASHR:v1p239/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p239/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p239/r3.claim: Waqf is stopping the voice long enough to breathe, intending to resume from the stopped word or what precedes it, not to abandon recitation.
NASHR:v1p239/r3.anchor: والوقف: عبارة عن قطع الصوت على الكلمة زمنا يتنفس فيه عادة بنية استئناف القراءة

NASHR:v1p239/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p239/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p239/r4.claim: Waqf takes a basmala at surah openings, may occur at verse ends and within verses, never inside a word or across joined orthography, and requires breath.
NASHR:v1p239/r4.anchor: وتنبغي البسملة معه في فواتح السور كما سيأتي ويأتي في رءوس الآي وأوساطها، ولا يأتي في وسط كلمة

NASHR:v1p239/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p239/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p239/r5.claim: Sakt is a shorter interruption than waqf, without breathing; authorities describe its duration variously from brief to long enough to seem forgotten.
NASHR:v1p239/r5.anchor: والسكت: هو عبارة عن قطع الصوت زمنا هو دون زمن الوقف عادة من غير تنفس

JISHUMI:v1p598/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r1.claim: Ibrahim accepted the truth once its proof was clear, resisting desire and habit; believers should accept truth without obstinacy.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r1.anchor: الآية تدل على حسن إجابة إبراهيم وقبوله ما أمر به لما وضحت الحجة

JISHUMI:v1p598/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r2.claim: God selected Ibrahim because he answered what he was charged with and carried it out well.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r2.anchor: وتدل على أنه إنما اصطفاه لإجابته إلى ما كلف وحسن قيامه به

JISHUMI:v1p598/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r3.claim: The verse indicates prophets are protected from sin and purified, which makes divine selection fitting.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r3.anchor: وتدل على كون الأنبياء معصومين منزهين؛ لذلك صح الاصطفاء.

JISHUMI:v1p598/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر
JISHUMI:v1p598/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, and Ibn ʿĀmir read وأوصى with an initial alif, matching the codices of Medina and Syria; the others read وَوَصَّى with gemination.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر: وأوصى بالألف، وكذلك في مصاحف المدينة والشام،

JISHUMI:v1p598/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r5.claim: The two readings have the same sense, but وصّى conveys greater emphasis and repetition.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r5.anchor: المعنى واحد، إلا أن في وصى مبالغة وتكثيرا.

JISHUMI:v1p598/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r6.claim: وصّى and أوصى are equivalent forms; waṣiyya means a command to obey.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r6.anchor: وصى وأوصى نظائر، والوصية: الأمر بالطاعة.

JISHUMI:v1p598/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r7.claim: On one parsing, Yaʿqub is nominative as a coordinate of Ibrahim: Ibrahim and Yaʿqub both enjoined their sons.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r7.anchor: يعقوب: رفع؛ لأنه عطف على إبراهيم، كأنه قيل: وصى إبراهيم ويعقوب،

JISHUMI:v1p598/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r8.claim: Alternatively, Yaʿqub begins an independent clause, meaning that Yaʿqub enjoined his sons.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r8.anchor: وقيل: على الاستئناف، فكأنه قيل: ووصى يعقوب بنيه.

JISHUMI:v1p598/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r9.claim: The definite article in al-dīn refers to the known religion, Islam, rather than religion generically.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r9.anchor: للعهد لا للجنس، ولأنه لم يختر لهم جميع الأديان، وإنما اختار دين الإسلام

JISHUMI:v1p598/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r10.claim: The passage follows the account of Ibrahim's concern for his descendants' welfare and prayers for them, then stresses his concern for religion.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r10.anchor: لما بين تعالى شدة محبة إبراهيم وذريته، وما يعود إلى صلاحهم، وأنه دعا لهم بما تقدم،

JISHUMI:v1p598/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r11.speaker: أبو علي والزجاج
JISHUMI:v1p598/r11.claim: The pronoun refers to the previously mentioned religious way; the author prefers this explicit reading because it includes the other proposed referents.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r11.anchor: قيل: بالملة، وقد تقدم ذكرها، فرجعت الكناية إليه، عن أبي علي والزجاج،

JISHUMI:v1p598/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r12.speaker: أبو القاسم وبريدة
JISHUMI:v1p598/r12.claim: They explain the pronoun as the words “I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds,” made an enduring word among Ibrahim's descendants.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r12.anchor: الكلمة التي هي قوله: (أسلمت لرب العالمين) حكاه أبو القاسم وبريدة،

JISHUMI:v1p598/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r13.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
JISHUMI:v1p598/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil identify it as the word of sincerity, “There is no god but God.”
JISHUMI:v1p598/r13.anchor: وقيل: بكلمة الإخلاص: لا إله إلا الله، عن ابن عباس ومقاتل.

JISHUMI:v1p598/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r14.claim: Ibrahim singled out his sons because his concern for them was greater and they were especially suited to receive the counsel, though he prayed for Islam for everyone.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r14.anchor: إنما خص البنين؛ لأن إشفاقه عليهم أكثر، والوصية بهم أليق، وهم إلى قبوله أليق،

JISHUMI:v1p598/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p598/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Yaʿqub and Esau were twins; Esau came first and Yaʿqub followed, holding his heel, which explains Yaʿqub's name.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r15.anchor: وسمي يعقوب؛ لأنه وعيصو كانا توأمين، فتقدم عيصو، وخرج يعقوب على أثره، آخذا بعقبه، عن ابن عباس،

JISHUMI:v1p598/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r16.claim: Yaʿqub enjoined his twelve sons, the tribes.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r16.anchor: والمعنى وصى يعقوب بنيه الاثني عشر، وهم الأسباط

JISHUMI:v1p598/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r17.claim: “O my sons” is parsed as if introduced by أن; it is omitted because the testament is speech.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r17.anchor: تقديره: أن يا بني فحذف (أن) لأن الوصية قول

JISHUMI:v1p598/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p598/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p598/r18.claim: The author cites 33:29 as another example of حذف أن after a verb of saying or promising.
JISHUMI:v1p598/r18.anchor: كقوله: (وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات منهم مغفرة وأجرا عظيما (29)

JISHUMI:v1p599/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p599/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p599/r1.claim: One explanation is that God purified and distinguished the religion through proofs until it became clear to anyone seeking it.
JISHUMI:v1p599/r1.anchor: استخلصه، وميزه بالأدلة، حتى اتضح وتجلى لمن طلب

JISHUMI:v1p599/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p599/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p599/r2.claim: Another explanation is that God chose the religion for them; the definite article refers to the known religion, Islam.
JISHUMI:v1p599/r2.anchor: اختار لكم الدين، والألف واللام للعهد، وأراد دين الإسلام

JISHUMI:v1p599/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p599/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p599/r3.claim: The prohibition concerns abandoning Islam, not dying; they must remain Muslim so death finds them in that state.
JISHUMI:v1p599/r3.anchor: النهي عن ترك الإسلام، لا عن الموت، وإن اتصل في اللفظ، وتقديره لا تتركوا الإسلام،

JISHUMI:v1p599/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p599/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p599/r4.claim: An alternative paraphrase is not to expose oneself to dying while leaving Islam through unbelief.
JISHUMI:v1p599/r4.anchor: لا تتعرضوا للموت على ترك الإسلام بفعل الكفر،

JISHUMI:v1p599/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p599/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p599/r5.claim: The construction resembles “do not let me see you here”: it forbids being there in a way that results in being seen.
JISHUMI:v1p599/r5.anchor: ونظيره لا أرينك ههنا، أي لا تتعرض لأن أراك ههنا،

JISHUMI:v1p599/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p599/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p599/r6.claim: One gloss of Muslims here is sincere.

JISHUMI:v1p599/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p599/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p599/r7.claim: Another gloss is believers who submit obediently.

JISHUMI:v1p599/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p599/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p599/r8.claim: The verse indicates that Islam was the way followed by Ibrahim's descendants.
JISHUMI:v1p599/r8.anchor: الآية تدل على أن الإسلام كان طريقة ذرية إبراهيم

JISHUMI:v1p600/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p600/r1.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v1p600/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God prescribed a deathbed testament, and Yaʿqub had nothing else to bequeath them except piety.
JISHUMI:v1p600/r1.anchor: قال الحسن: كتب الله الوصية عند الموت، ولم يكن له شيء أن يوصيهم بتقوى الله.

BURHAN:v1p168/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p168/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p168/r1.claim: Alif and lam occur frequently in Qur'anic openings because they are common letters in speech.
BURHAN:v1p168/r1.anchor: فلأن الألف واللام كثرت فى الفواتح دون غيرها من الحروف لكثرتها فى الكلام

BURHAN:v1p168/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p168/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p168/r2.claim: The opening letters also carry articulatory significance: hamza is deepest, lam is made at the tongue tip against the upper palate, and mim at the closed lips.
BURHAN:v1p168/r2.anchor: أن الهمزة من الرئة فهى أعمق الحروف واللام مخرجها من طرف اللسان ملصقة بصدر الغار الأعلى من الفم

BURHAN:v1p168/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p168/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p168/r3.claim: Those letters can stand for the rest, just as the testimony of faith entails its other requirements, alluded to in the Prophet's command to fight until people affirm God's oneness.
BURHAN:v1p168/r3.anchor: ويرمز بهن إلى باقى الحروف كما رمز صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا لا إله إلا الله

BURHAN:v1p168/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p168/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p168/r4.claim: The pairing of ta with sin and ha is meaningful: ta gathers five articulatory qualities, while sin is its contrasting unvoiced, soft, sibilant counterpart.
BURHAN:v1p168/r4.anchor: فإن الطاء جمعت من صفات الحروف خمس صفات لم يجمعها غيرها وهى الجهر والشدة والاستعلاء والإطباق والإصمات

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r1.claim: Earlier scholars often used waqf, qaṭʿ, and sakt interchangeably for stopping; later scholars distinguished their technical meanings.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r1.anchor: الوقف والقطع والسكت عبارات يطلقها المتقدمون غالبا مرادا بها الوقف والمتأخرون فرقوا فقالوا

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r2.claim: Qaṭʿ ends recitation altogether, as though the reader has finished and turned to another activity; it is made only at a verse ending.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r2.anchor: فالقارئ به كالمعرض عن القراءة والمنتقل إلى حالة أخرى غيرها

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r3.speaker: ابن أبي الهذيل
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl reports a sound narration that they disliked reciting part of a verse and leaving the rest; al-Suyuti infers the plural refers to Companions.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي الهذيل أنه قال كانوا يكرهون أن يقرؤوا بعض الآية ويدعوا بعضها إسناده صحيح

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r4.claim: Waqf briefly interrupts the voice, usually for a breath, to resume recitation rather than abandon it; it can occur at verse ends or within verses, but not within a word or joined spelling.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r4.anchor: والوقف عبارة عن قطع الصوت عن الكلمة زمنا يتنفس فيه عادة بنية استئناف القراءة

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r5.claim: Sakt is a shorter voice break than waqf, without breathing.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r5.anchor: والسكت عبارة عن قطع الصوت زمنا هو دون زمن الوقف عادة من غير تنفس

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r6.speaker: حمزة
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r6.claim: Hamza describes the pause before a hamza after a vowelless letter as slight.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r6.anchor: فعن حمزة في السكت على الساكن قبل الهمزة سكتة يسيرة

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r7.speaker: الأشناني
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r7.claim: Al-Ashnani describes the pause as short.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r7.anchor: وقال الاشناني قصيرة وعن الكسائي سكتة مختلسة

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r8.speaker: الكسائي
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r8.claim: Al-Kisa'i describes sakt as quickly taken, without lengthening.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r8.anchor: وعن الكسائي سكتة مختلسة من غير إشباع

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r9.speaker: ابن غلبون
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r9.claim: Ibn Ghalbun calls it a brief pause.

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r10.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r10.claim: Makki calls it a light pause.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r10.anchor: وقال ابن غلبون وقفة يسيرة وقال مكي وقفة خفيفة

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r11.speaker: ابن شريح
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r11.claim: Ibn Shurayh calls it a tiny pause.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r11.anchor: وقال ابن شريح وقيفة وعن قتيبة من غير قطع نفس

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r12.speaker: قتيبة
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r12.claim: Qutayba describes it as a pause without cutting the breath.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r12.anchor: وعن قتيبة من غير قطع نفس وقال الداني سكتة لطيفة

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r13.speaker: الداني
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r13.claim: Al-Dani calls it a delicate pause without cutting the breath.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r13.anchor: وقال الداني سكتة لطيفة من غير قطع

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r14.speaker: الجعبري
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r14.claim: Al-Ja'bari defines sakt as a short voice break less than the time needed to exhale; if prolonged, it becomes waqf.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r14.anchor: وقال الجعبري قطع الصوت زمنا قليلا أقصر من زمن إخراج النفس لأنه أن طال صار وقفا

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r15.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r15.claim: Ibn al-Jazari holds that sakt is governed by transmitted recitation and is allowed only where a sound report supports an intended meaning.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r15.anchor: قال ابن الجزري والصحيح أنه مقيد بالسماع والنقل ولا يجوز إلا فيما صحت الرواية به

ITQAN:v1p233#2/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r16.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r16.claim: Another view permits sakt at verse endings while continuing, to clarify meaning; some interpret the transmitted hadith accordingly.
ITQAN:v1p233#2/r16.anchor: وقيل يجوز في رؤوس الآي مطلقا حالة الوصل لقصد البيان وحمل بعضهم الحديث الوارد على ذلك

ITQAN:v2p440#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r1.speaker: سيبويه
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r1.claim: Sibawayh says al- replaces the deleted hamza in the original ilāh; al-Farisi cites the article's fixed form and the hamza's cut pronunciation as evidence.
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r1.anchor: فقال سيبويه هي عوض من الهمزة المحذوفة بناء على أن أصله إله

ITQAN:v2p440#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r2.speaker: آخرون
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r2.claim: Others treat al- as a definite article added for glorification, deriving ilāh from lāh.
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون هي مزيدة للتعريف تفخيما وتعظيما وأصل إله لاه

ITQAN:v2p440#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r3.speaker: قوم
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r3.claim: A group says al- is an inseparable addition, not a marker of definiteness.
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r3.anchor: وقال قوم هي زائدة لازمة لا للتعريف

ITQAN:v2p440#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r4.claim: Some derive the form from the written hāʾ, then a possessive lām, followed by al- for exaltation and emphasis.
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم أصله هاء الكتابة زيدت فيه لام الملك فصار له

ITQAN:v2p440#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r5.speaker: الخليل
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r5.claim: Al-Khalil and others say the name is indivisible, a proper name with no derivation or prior root.
ITQAN:v2p440#2/r5.anchor: وقال الخليل وخلائق هي من بنية الكلمة وهو اسم علم لا اشتقاق له ولا أصل

ITQAN:v2p495/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p495/r1.speaker: ابن هشام
ITQAN:v2p495/r1.claim: Ibn Hisham says al-Zamakhshari's explanation is not the only possible analysis: tanwin may replace an added verse-final lengthening letter, then be joined as if pausing.
ITQAN:v2p495/r1.anchor: قال ابن هشام وليس التوجيه منحصرا عند الزمخشري في ذلك بل جوز كون التنوين بدلا من حرف الإطلاق المزيد في رأس الآية

ITQAN:v3p270/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p270/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p270/r1.claim: One listed kind of word-form change is altering the structure, illustrated by Ṭūr Sīnīn, whose original form is given as Sīnā.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r1.claim: Jurjānī says familiar comparisons praise clear, smooth, sweet wording: it is intelligible, unambiguous, familiar, and free of sound clusters that strain the tongue.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r1.anchor: ألفاظه كالماء في السلاسة وكالنسيم في الرقة وكالعسل في الحلاوة يريدون أن اللفظ لا يستغلق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r2.claim: These analogies require a subtle interpretive return from one thing to another, more than the obvious comparison of an argument to the sun.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r2.anchor: فهذا كله تأول ورد شىء إلى شىء بضرب من التلطف وهو ادخل قليلا في حقيقة التأول

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r3.speaker: كعب الاشقري
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r3.claim: Asked by al-Ḥajjāj about the sons of al-Muhallab, Kaʿb described them as day guardians and night cavalry, comparing their unity to a ring without a discernible end.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r3.anchor: كعب الاشقري وقد أوفده المهلب على الحجاج فوصف له بنيه وذكر مكانهم من الفضل والبأس

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r4.claim: The unbroken-ring comparison is not understood fully by immediate hearing; it needs an alert, discerning mind above the ordinary audience.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r4.anchor: لا يفهمه حق فهمه إلا من له ذهن ونظر يرتفع به عن طبقة العامة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r5.claim: Smoothness comparisons can occur in ordinary speech, whereas the subtle ring image belongs to wisdom and refined writing by people of mature intellect.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p73/r5.anchor: فأما ما كان مذهبه اللطف مذهب قوله هم كالحلقة فلا تراه إلا في الآداب والحكم المأثورة عن الفضلاء

ITQAN:v4p384/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p384/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p384/r7.claim: The sons of Abraham named here are Ismail, Ishaq, Madyan, Zamran, Sarh, Nafsh, Nafshan, Umaym, Kaysan, Surah, Lutan, and Nafish.
ITQAN:v4p384/r7.anchor: هم إسماعيل وإسحاق ومدين وزمران وسرح ونفش ونفشان وأميم وكيسان وسورح ولوطان ونافش

ITQAN:v1p252/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p252/r4.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p252/r4.claim: Mīm before bā is hidden with nasalization after a vowel, but pronounced clearly after sukūn; Ibn al-Jazari says listing this as idghām, as earlier scholars did, is incorrect because it is ikhfāʾ.
ITQAN:v1p252/r4.anchor: وهذا نوع من الإخفاء المذكور في الترجمة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f4.claim: The Quran uses waṣṣā (with gemination) for religious and moral matters, but awṣā for material matters such as inheritance.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f4.anchor: فكل ما ورد فيه من (وصّى) بالتشديد فهو في الدين والأمور المعنوية، وكل ما ورد من (أوصى) فهو في الأمور المادية
